transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor... I came in because of my in-laws. I know they aren't just arguing with me anymore. They're actually using the altar and the parish committee to push me out. It's like they are trying to make everyone completely forget what I have done for this family over the years.
When you say they're using the altar and parish committee to push you out, do you have specific examples of things they've said or done that made you realize this plan?

Well, like I was just saying, it's... it's just obvious to me. I don't have a recording of them saying it out loud, but I know exactly what they are doing. They get up there by the altar, or they whisper with the parish committee, and the whole point is to push me out. They want to make sure every single person forgets all the hard work and... everything I've done for this family over the years. It's not just regular family arguing anymore, I just know it's a whole plan against me.
How long have you been noticing this plan by your in-laws to push you out? Did this feeling come on suddenly, or has it been building up over time?

It has been going on for about two months now. This whole crisis... it really started right after we had a big fight over the Día de los Muertos altar. That is when it all began. So, I guess it started then, about two months ago, and they've been doing it ever since.
Before these two months started, were you able to work, take care of your responsibilities, and get along with your family without these kinds of concerns about plans against you?

Well, before two months ago, things were mostly fine. I was doing everything I normally do. But since this all started... I just haven't been able to keep up with any of it. I stopped being able to help with the parish preparations, which I always do. I can't even manage the house the way I usually do. 

My family actually had to step in and take over all the festival tasks because I just... couldn't. And my husband, he's been staying really close to me lately. He noticed I was missing meals and just forgetting my normal routines. I guess I haven't really been taking care of myself reliably since this whole thing with my in-laws began.
Besides knowing what your in-laws are planning, have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people around you don't seem to notice or hear?

Well, yes, actually. I... I have been hearing things. On several nights recently, I heard my late mother's voice. It was clear as day, telling me exactly where to put the marigolds and the candles for the altar. And then... well, one time, I even saw her. She was just standing right near the kitchen doorway. I told my husband, but he looked and said there was no one there. But I know I saw her.
During the times when you're hearing your mother's voice or seeing her, are you able to think clearly and remember what's happening around you, or do you feel confused or like things are foggy?

I don't feel confused when it happens. My mind feels pretty clear, actually. I know where I am, I remember what I'm doing... it's just that I hear her, or see her. Everything else around me seems perfectly normal, not foggy at all.
When you hear your mother's voice or see her in the kitchen, do you think these experiences are real, or do you recognize that they might not be happening the way they seem to you?

Well, to me, they are completely real. Like I said, I heard her voice very clearly on those nights, telling me exactly where the marigolds and candles should go. And that time I saw her standing by the kitchen doorway... she was right there. My husband told me no one was there, but I know what I saw and heard. It doesn't feel like my mind is playing tricks on me at all.

Looking back at everything you've told me - the plan by your in-laws, hearing your mother's voice, seeing her by the kitchen - do you ever wonder if any of these things might not be exactly as they seem, or are you completely certain they are all real and happening?

I... no, I don't really wonder about that. I'm completely certain it's all real. I know what I saw and heard with my mother. 

And as for the rest of it... well, that's the whole reason I came in. I knew my in-laws were not just arguing with me over nothing. It's obvious they are using the altar and the parish committee to push me out. They are trying to make everyone forget what I have done for this family. So, yes, I'm sure it's all exactly as I'm telling you.

If your husband or a doctor told you that what you're experiencing with your mother's voice and the things your in-laws are doing might not be real, would you be able to consider that they might be right, or are you absolutely certain no matter what anyone says?

I wouldn't believe them. I know what I'm experiencing is real. Like I said before, that's exactly why I'm here. I know my in-laws aren't just having normal arguments with me. It's completely clear to me that they're using the altar situation and the parish committee to deliberately push me out. They want to erase everything I've done for this family, make everyone forget my contributions. No matter what a doctor or my husband says, I know what they're doing to me is real.

In the month or two before the big fight over the Día de los Muertos altar, did you notice anything unusual happening - even small things like feeling suspicious about people's intentions, or sensing that something was off, even if you didn't have the full picture of what was going on?

No, I don't think so. Everything seemed pretty normal before the altar situation came up. I mean, we've always had regular family disagreements here and there, but I didn't feel suspicious of them or sense that anything was wrong before that. 

It really just started when they began interfering with the Día de los Muertos preparations. That's when it became obvious what they were doing. But in the months before that... no, nothing was off.

In that week or two right before the big fight over the Día de los Muertos altar, did you notice anything strange about how you were perceiving things - like colors seeming brighter, sounds seeming louder, or feeling like you were noticing details that others weren't picking up on?

Um... no, I didn't notice anything like that. The colors and sounds were just normal. I wasn't picking up on any special details or anything like that, either. Like I was saying, everything was just regular everyday life until they started interfering with the altar.

When you think back to that week right after the big fight over the Día de los Muertos altar, did the hearing of your mother's voice and seeing her start suddenly - like all at once - or did it come on more gradually over several days or a week or two?

It started pretty suddenly, right after that argument. Just over the next few days... well, on several nights, I heard my late mother's voice. She was talking to me, telling me exactly where to put the marigolds and the candles for the altar. 

And then one time, I actually saw her. She was just standing right near the kitchen doorway. My husband was there with me and he said no one was there, but I know I saw her. So, yes, it all happened pretty quickly right after that fight.
When your husband looked at the kitchen doorway and told you he didn't see your mother standing there, how did that make you feel about what you had just seen?

Well, I... I knew what I saw. I mean, like I said, I had already been hearing her voice on several nights, telling me exactly where to put the marigolds and the candles. So when I saw her standing right there near the kitchen doorway, it just... it made sense to me. 

When my husband said no one was there, I just thought he couldn't see her. But I know I did. It was clear as day to me, even if he couldn't see it.

When your husband looked at that same spot by the kitchen doorway and saw nothing, did that make you question whether what you saw was actually real, or did you feel certain that you had really seen your mother even though he couldn't see her?

I was completely certain. I didn't question it at all. Like I mentioned, I had already been hearing her voice on several different nights, telling me exactly where to place the marigolds and the candles for the altar. So when I saw her standing right there by the kitchen doorway, I knew it was her. Even though my husband said no one was there, I know what I saw and heard. It was real to me.

In the month or two before the big fight over the Día de los Muertos altar, did you notice that you were having any trouble concentrating, or that your thoughts felt scattered or harder to organize than usual?

No, I don't think so. In the months before that... well, everything seemed pretty normal. I wasn't having any trouble focusing or keeping my thoughts straight. My mind felt fine back then, so I didn't notice anything like that.

In the weeks right before or right after that big fight over the Día de los Muertos altar, did you notice that you needed less sleep than usual, or that you felt unusually energetic or like you were able to do a lot more than you normally can?

Yes, actually. Right around that time, I just couldn't stay still. I didn't feel tired at all. I kept cleaning the house, calling people on the phone, rewriting all the menus for the gathering... I was constantly moving boxes of decorations around. Everyone kept telling me I needed to sit down and rest, but I just felt like I had to keep going. I had all this energy and just couldn't stop doing things.
In that time right around the big fight over the Día de los Muertos altar, did you feel like you were unusually confident or that you had special abilities or insights that other people didn't have?

Well, yes, I did. I just... I truly believed that I was the only one who could save our family's traditions. It felt so clear to me at the time. I was absolutely certain that if people would just listen to me and do things my way, the whole community event would turn out perfect. I felt very sure of myself about all of it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with acute onset of delusions (persecution by in-laws using altar/parish committee) and hallucinations (auditory: mother's voice; visual: mother at kitchen doorway) occurring over approximately 2 months following a clear psychosocial stressor (fight over Día de los Muertos altar). The acute presentation with rapid symptom development, preserved sensorium and orientation, lack of preceding prodromal symptoms, and significant functional impairment are consistent with Brief Psychotic Disorder or First-Episode Psychosis. The 2-month duration and absence of mood episodes make F23.9 (Unspecified Acute Psychotic Disorder) most appropriate, though F22.9 (Delusional Disorder) and F20.0 (Paranoid Schizophrenia) remain differential considerations pending longer observation.
